metaDescription: The number is not the intelligence. The connection is. BUY · LABOR · SELL · RECOVER are economic lenses over one hospitality operating model.
heroTitleLine1: The number is not the intelligence.
heroLead: RADR connects what you buy, who works, what you sell and what should have been recovered — then finds where those relationships change contribution.

buy.title: Stop leaking value before it hits the P&L.
buy.lead: Supplier systems, invoices, contracts and deliveries become one decision story: variance detected, credit prepared, value verified.

labor.title: Staff to demand. Not to guesswork.
labor.lead: Forecast demand against the current roster. Catch over and under staffing early, prepare the adjustment, protect margin — without another scheduling product.

sell.title: Know where revenue becomes margin.
sell.lead: Sales, channel mix, discounts, menu contribution and delivery commissions, compared across locations with money attached and a clear next decision.

recover.title: What you're owed shouldn't disappear.
recover.lead: Supplier credits, refunds, late cancellations, inventory recovery and uncollected value, carried until observed proof — Verified Value, not a hopeful estimate.

industriesLead: Not every venue. Operations with enough complexity that margin disappears between systems.

restaurants.title: Restaurant groups
restaurants.lead: Multi-unit dining portfolios: city concepts, regional groups, international brands. Shared suppliers, shared labor markets, one language for margin.

hotels.title: Hotels
hotels.lead: Rooms and F&B as one operating picture. Banqueting, outlets, procurement and labor finally sit in the same financial truth.

destination.title: Destination hospitality
destination.lead: Resorts, private clubs and venue groups: high-stakes service, complex spend, and recovery that cannot wait for month-end.

operations.title: Independent operators
operations.lead: One location. The same financial discipline as a group: spend, labor, sales and recovery in one operating view.

groups.title: Hospitality groups
groups.lead: Compare locations and control margin across the portfolio: one language from site to finance.

cfo.title: Finance & operations
cfo.lead: One operating truth between the floor and the P&L: findings with money attached, Prepared Actions with owners, value that can be verified.

intelligence.title: Built around your operation.
intelligence.lead: Every hospitality business runs differently. RADR understands the systems, economics and decisions that matter to yours.
intelligence.domainsNote: Domain model, not a live connector claim. Status marks what exists today.
intelligence.workRemovedNote: Preparation and monitoring first. External execution only where systems and policy support it.
intelligence.disclaimer: Illustrative operating models. Detectors and connectors ship by domain over time.

restaurants.headline: Restaurant economics, read as one operation.
restaurants.lead: Covers, labor, menu mix, supplier invoices and delivery are not separate tools. They are one money story for the night.
restaurants.edge: RADR watches booking pace against staffing, invoice lines against contracts, and menu contribution against volume.

labor.summary: Service pressure · kitchen 94% · adding FOH feeds the bottleneck · Berlin Mitte
labor.action: Move 1 FOH to bar · slow delivery 25m

recover.summary: A late cancellation released a four top. RADR identified replacement demand and the table was rebooked.
recover.action: Keep recovery workflow on for peak cancellations.

buy.summary: Tuna Tataki bestseller · 6 portions short for peak · Berlin Mitte
buy.action: Feature Truffle Pasta first · supplier fallback

sell.summary: Two high volume menu items are generating strong revenue but below target contribution margin.
evidence: Food cost drift on both recipes
sell.action: Review portion and pricing on the two items before the weekend.

capacity.summary: Empty tables ≠ capacity · 38 covers inbound · kitchen 92% · Berlin Mitte
evidence: Delivery +31% vs plan · 9 second-turn tables at risk
capacity.action: Wait 12 minutes · throttle delivery · feature fast dish

hotels.headline: Hotel economics, not a restaurant model in different clothes.
hotels.lead: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, channel mix, housekeeping and room inventory move money differently from covers and table turns.
hotels.edge: RADR reasons across rooms, distribution, labor and ancillary spend so rate, recovery and cost sit in one operating picture.

sell.summary: 89% occupancy · OTA share +11 pts · hold direct vs release OTA
sell.action: Review premium room pricing for remaining inventory.

recover.summary: Six cancelled rooms for this weekend have returned to inventory. Current pickup suggests four are likely to refill naturally. Two remain financially exposed.
evidence: Channel mix favors OTA refill unless direct offers run
recover.action: Release a targeted direct offer on the two exposed rooms.

buy.summary: Laundry cost per occupied room increased 11% this month without a corresponding occupancy or contract change.
evidence: Variance concentrated in towel and sheet lines
buy.action: Open a cost review with the laundry vendor this week.

labor.summary: Housekeeping hours scheduled tomorrow exceed modeled room turnover demand.
labor.action: Trim two housekeeping shifts before the morning briefing.

bars.headline: Daypart economics for bars and cafés.
bars.lead: Hourly sales, product mix, waste and weather move cash differently than a full-service dining room.
bars.edge: RADR watches ticket size, staffing and inventory against the conditions that actually drive the daypart.

sell.summary: Warm afternoon conditions historically increase terrace demand, while current staffing and inventory remain planned to the indoor baseline.
evidence: Historical terrace lift on comparable days
sell.action: Staff the terrace for peak and stage high velocity terrace SKUs.

buy.summary: Coffee supplier pricing differs from the agreed August price book.
buy.action: Request a credit against the August price book.

labor.summary: Tuesday afternoon labor is scheduled above demand observed across comparable weeks.
evidence: Hours scheduled: flat to last week
labor.action: Cut one afternoon shift or move coverage to evening peak.

groups.headline: One operating truth across every location.
groups.lead: Portfolio value is not a ranking table. It is understanding why locations differ, then acting on the drivers.
groups.edge: RADR decomposes performance so an executive can move from group to region to location to finding to evidence.

portfolio.summary: Amsterdam Zuid is outperforming De Pijp by €4,200 this week.
portfolio.why: The strongest driver is dinner traffic between Thursday and Saturday. Labor productivity explains another meaningful portion of the variance.
portfolio.action: Replicate Zuid dinner pacing and discount discipline at De Pijp for the next two weekends.
portfolio.path: Group → Amsterdam → De Pijp → Finding → Evidence

finance.headline: When operations and finance share one truth.
finance.lead: RADR connects invoices, contracts, labor, payments and POS so margin questions have money attached.
finance.edge: The point is not another dashboard. It is identified value, pending verification and verified outcomes in one ledger.

month.summary: Operational and financial signals reconciled into one identified value total.
month.action: Clear the three awaiting-action findings before month close.
month.questions: Where are we leaking money? Which invoices miss contracts? How much value has RADR verified?

apartments.headline: This empty Tuesday isn’t random.
apartments.lead: Orphan gaps look random until comparable history and release conditions are modeled together.
apartments.edge: Wait · discount · direct first · OTA first — with net contribution attached.

sell.summary: 17 comparable orphan gaps · 64% historical fill under relevant release condition
sell.action: Review premium room pricing for remaining inventory.

recover.action: Release a targeted direct offer on the two exposed rooms.

evidence: Variance concentrated in towel and sheet lines
buy.action: Open a cost review with the laundry vendor this week.

labor.action: Trim two housekeeping shifts before the morning briefing.
